newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up strongly, seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up strongly, seen rising further.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose strongly in high volume on Tuesday on Russia's better than expected credit rating and President Boris Yeltsin's move from hospital, traders said.
They forecast a further rise in prices in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 3.91 percent to 169.90 on $27.06 million in volume.
"Everything is rising on the news about the rating and Yeltsin's health," said Alexei Goncharov, head of information department at Russian Brokerage House.
On Monday IBCA, Moody's and Standard & Poor's assigned Russia better than expected ratings for its first Eurobond.

Yeltsin also moved from hospital where he was preparing for a heart operation to the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow, where he will be working and walking. Doctors said his condition was quite satisfactory.
Alexander Bubnovsky, a trader from Alfa-Capital, explained the rise by an inflow of small but frequent orders from the West.
"Those who have not yet bought enough paper in Russia are buying, those who were selling are now buying not to miss the rally," he said.
He forecast a small rise in the one to two percent range in the next few days. Goncharov said the gainers of the day were energy shares and LUKoil.
He attributed the LUKoil rise to arbitration deals with its American Depositary Receipts on the Berlin Bourse.
First half results from Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz did not have an impact on the market, Goncharov said.
Konpetroleum posted a first half year pretax loss of 466 billion roubles and Varyoganneftegaz's first half loss was 80 billion roubles.
Mosenergo was traded at $0.945 after $0.879 at Monday's close, Lukoil rose to $9.85 from $9.24, Gazprom rose to $0.430 from $0.373 and Norilsk Nickel was $6.30 after $6.13.
